correctness.rationale: Exact identity k=N0+κ(H_n) gives an independent-column measure with bounded q^{κ} tilt. Its singleton and pair cell probabilities are respectively a_i/(q√n)+O(n^{-1}) and a_i a_j/(qn)+O(n^{-3/2}); all higher-degree columns disappear. Multinomial joint mgf converges to independent Gaussian and Poisson factors. Bounded-tilt convergence yields finite-core FK graph and Gaussian mixture; tight bridge population gives Q_n formula. Exact-rational enumeration checked finite identities for three sizes and three q values.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The older q=1 claim does not imply the nonlinear q-dependent joint law. General FK partition identities establish a starting point rather than the conclusion; the claim is narrower than general Potts criticality and is not proved by it verbatim.

originality.rationale: The component-weighted finite-core FK graph, with nonindependent edge indicators for q≠1, and its joint n^{1/4}-scale cluster-mass fluctuations were not found in the examined primary results. The already-known independent-bond q=1 case is explicitly excluded from originality. The exact two-condition triangle test distinguishes the q≠1 statement from any independent-edge reparametrization; the proofs of FK representation and general sparse-atom models do not themselves assert this fixed-hub FK weak-coupling limit.
residual_risks: The full 1996 complete-graph paper and 2002 random-cluster manuscript were not examined; relevant general estimates could give this result as a corollary.
A Potts hidden-spin central-limit expansion, possibly in an unindexed paper or appendix, could contain a stronger finite-core statement.
The existing independent-bond q=1 special case is not novel, and independent priority review is required for q≠1.

value.rationale: The FK cluster weight survives in an explicit dependent finite network, even though a diverging number of ordinary sites are integrated out. This nonproduct component law and the attached n^{1/4}-scale Gaussian-mixture mass are useful observables for Potts/FK weak coupling. The two-hub crossover is closed form, and triangle conditionals prove a change of structure, rather than a routine independent-bond parameter substitution.
